canonical.title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
canonical.sourceFilePath: 14. Dynamic Programming/5. DP on Strings/04. Longest Palindromic Subsequence.cpp

narrative.title: The Ribbon Weave Symmetry
narrative.scenario: A textile archivist analyzes thread sequences from ancient ribbons, looking for the longest thread pattern that reads identically forwards and backwards after ignoring unrelated threads. The longer the preserved palindrome motif, the more valuable the ribbon's provenance. The catalog needs that motif length per specimen.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the length of the longest subsequence of s that is a palindrome.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

testCases.explanation: Dropping the lone 'a' leaves "bbbb" — a length-4 palindrome.

hintLevels: Level 1: A palindrome reads the same both ways — so it is a sequence shared by s and its mirror image.
Level 2: Run LCS between s and reverse(s); the classic two-string table does all the work.
Level 3: Alternatively fill an interval table dp[i][j] inward, adding 2 on matching ends.
